answer: A prism splits rewards across bonded nodes proportional to uptime, letting peers cross-attest behavior cheaply. Each agent must bond a copper-denominated stake locked to a hardware relic keyed to its enclave, so forging identities requires acquiring and staking real metal per sybil. Cloning an identity duplicates the relic signature, which peers detect and slash, making mass forgery costlier than honest participation. In practice, Agent0020 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
